skill.name: stable-baselines3
skill.description: Build and evaluate reinforcement learning workflows with Stable Baselines3. The skill covers algorithm selection, Gymnasium environments, callbacks, vectorized training, model persistence, and performance evaluation.
skill.summary: Create reliable Stable Baselines3 training, environment, monitoring, and evaluation workflows.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Reinforcement learning projects often fail because algorithm choice, environment contracts, and evaluation workflows are inconsistent. This skill provides practical Stable Baselines3 guidance and reusable training templates.
actual_capabilities: Selects suitable Stable Baselines3 algorithms for discrete, continuous, and goal-conditioned tasks.
Creates Gymnasium environment structures with valid observation, action, reset, and step contracts.
Builds training workflows with vectorized environments, evaluation callbacks, checkpoints, and TensorBoard logging.
Explains callback design for monitoring, early stopping, custom metrics, and training control.
Guides model saving, loading, normalization state handling, evaluation, comparison, and video recording.
Provides troubleshooting guidance for memory use, unstable learning, API mismatches, and parallel environments.
limitations: Stable Baselines3, Gymnasium, PyTorch, and optional recording dependencies must be installed separately.
The included scripts are templates and require adaptation for custom algorithms, policies, and environment behavior.
Training can consume significant CPU, GPU, memory, disk space, and time.
The guidance cannot guarantee convergence or replace task-specific reward design and statistical validation.

use_cases.title: Compare Learning Algorithms
use_cases.description: Select and compare algorithms using action-space requirements, sample efficiency, training stability, and compute limits.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Production Candidates
use_cases.description: Load checkpoints, apply normalization state, compare rewards, record behavior, and diagnose evaluation differences.

prompt_templates.title: Train a First Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PPO training workflow for CartPole-v1 with evaluation, checkpoints, TensorBoard logs, and dependency instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Custom Environment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Gymnasium environment for [problem], define spaces and rewards, validate it with check_env, and explain each design choice.

prompt_templates.title: Choose and Compare Algorithms
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare PPO, SAC, TD3, and DQN for [task], then recommend one based on action space, sample efficiency, and compute limits.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Advanced Training System
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an SB3 workflow with vectorization, normalization, custom callbacks, reproducible evaluation, checkpoint recovery, and performance diagnostics for [task].

output_examples.input: Recommend an algorithm for a continuous robotic control task with expensive simulations.
output: Primary recommendation: SAC for continuous actions and strong sample efficiency.
Use one to four environments and evaluate deterministic policies on separate episodes.
Consider TD3 when lower policy stochasticity is preferred.

output_examples.input: Outline a safe training workflow for a custom Gymnasium environment.
output: Define spaces and return values with consistent data types.
Run check_env before training and test random actions.
Add evaluation and checkpoint callbacks before long runs.
Measure performance across multiple evaluation episodes and seeds.

output_examples.input: Explain why vectorized evaluation differs from a standard Gymnasium loop.
output_examples.output: Vectorized environments return batched observations and four step values. They also reset completed environments automatically and expose terminal observations through the info data.

best_practices: Validate every custom environment with check_env before training.
Separate training and evaluation environments, and preserve normalization statistics with the model.
Use checkpoints, deterministic evaluation, multiple episodes, and fixed seeds for reproducible comparisons.
anti_patterns: Do not select an algorithm without checking the action space and policy requirements.
Do not judge performance from training rewards or a single evaluation episode.
Do not increase parallel environments without checking memory use, rollout size, and algorithm behavior.

faq.question: Which algorithms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers PPO, A2C, SAC, TD3, DDPG, DQN, HER, and related Stable Baselines3 workflows.

faq.question: Can it create a custom Gymnasium environment?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains required methods, spaces, validation, registration, rendering, testing, and Stable Baselines3 compatibility.

faq.question: Does it support parallel training?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers DummyVecEnv, SubprocVecEnv, environment counts, rollout sizing, normalization, and vectorized API differences.

faq.question: Can it monitor and stop training?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides callback guidance for evaluation, checkpoints, reward thresholds, custom metrics, progress, and early stopping.

faq.question: Does it evaluate and record trained agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers model loading, reward statistics, comparisons, rendering, normalization state, and video recording.

faq.question: Does it guarantee that an agent will learn?
faq.answer: No. Results depend on environment design, rewards, hyperparameters, algorithm fit, compute resources, and statistical evaluation.
